text:
Anya Patel: Heads-up — I'm planning a small canary for the new pii_scrub_v2 pipeline. Schedule: 2026-11-15 13:00 UTC, start at 5% traffic, ramp to 20% over 30m if metrics look good. Purpose: stricter PII token scrub + a shorter retention window fallback. Need quick ok from SRE/security/data-retention before I flip the flag.
Devon Li: Quick q — does this change the retention window for existing archived logs or just live-request retention? Also will user-level retention overrides still apply?
Anya Patel: It only affects the live processing pipeline and the temporary KV we keep for 24h -> shifting to 7d in the canary. It does NOT rewrite historical archives. User-level overrides remain respected; the flag toggles default behavior only.
Sanjay Rao: Security: we can greenlight a 5% canary if all scrubbed outputs are verified not to leak tokenized PII. Two asks: (1) add a metric for scrubbed_token_rate and failed_scrub_count, (2) keep audit-mode OFF during the canary — enabling audit-mode will write PII to audit logs and requires KMS HSM route to be validated.
Leah Kim: Ops: we can schedule 5% -> 20% ramp. I need the feature-flag key and the rollout config to wire into the rollout controller. Also confirm the alert thresholds you want for fast rollback.
Anya Patel: Flag/rollout snippet below (will also be in the PR):

```json
{
  "flag": "pii_scrub_v2_enabled",
  "canary": {
    "percent": 5,
    "ramp": 20,
    "ramp_minutes": 30,
    "audience": "canary-traffic-2026-11",
    "regions": ["us-west-2","eu-central-1"]
  },
  "retention": {
    "default_days": 7,
    "grace_days": 0
  },
  "kms_route": "primary-kms->hsm-fallback"
}
```

Anya Patel: Alerts for rollback: failed_scrub_count > 10 in 1m OR scrub_latency_p90 > 2s OR scrubed_token_rate drop > 30% relative to baseline. Ops, deploy-bot, can you schedule the canary window and set the autoscale guard?

Mike O'Connor: I'll add the metrics and a quick graph in Grafana. PR will add `pii_scrub.v2.scrubbed_token_rate`, `pii_scrub.v2.failed_scrub_count`, and `pii_scrub.v2.latency_p90`. I'll also add a temporary alert runbook and assign on-call.
deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled: job id ci-canary-177800, start 2026-11-15T13:00:00Z, 5% -> 20% ramp over 30m. Notifying on-call.

Devon Li: Thumbs: do we want a DB migration or config change to support `grace_days: 0`? I can PR a config default if needed.

Anya Patel: No DB migration for this change — it's purely config-driven. Devon, if you can PR the rollout config and the small flag gate in the runtime, that'd be great. I'll keep audit-mode off for prod canary; plan is to validate successful scrub metrics and then run an audit-mode dry-run in staging that writes to a local audit bucket using the HSM route.

Sanjay Rao: SGTM. One more security nit: ensure KMS fallback path is exercised in staging before we ever enable audit-mode in prod. If HSM path errors, audit-mode must be blocked automatically.

Leah Kim: Ops note: will set a canary kill-switch so we can drop back to 0% instantly. Also will set an automated fallback to `pii_scrub_v1` if failed_scrub_count spikes.

Anya Patel: Thanks all. I'll post the PR link once ready and tag the rollout doc. Leaving a checklist below:
- [ ] PR with rollout config (Devon)
- [ ] Metrics + dashboard (Mike)
- [ ] Staging HSM fallback run (Sanjay)
- [ ] Ops guard + kill-switch (Leah)
- [ ] Final signoff and flip (Anya)

Mike O'Connor: I'll have the dashboard up by EOD today. :thumbsup:

Devon Li: PR opened: https://git.redwood.internal/p/1234 — includes flag gate + config. Please review.

Anya Patel: Reviewing now. If no objections by 11:30 UTC tomorrow, I'll kick the canary. Thanks! :eyes:
